note: Everything here is invented for testing. Any match with a real person, company or product is coincidental. Public product names (Supabase, Stripe, Gumroad, Firebase, Clerk) are used as ordinary public references.

A.summary: Frontend-strong builder. Has never handled payments or messaging at volume.

records.text: Frontend: React and TypeScript for 6 years. Comfortable with design systems, accessibility and browser performance.
Backend: has written small Node.js APIs and used Firebase and Supabase. Has never run a production server or a database migration alone.
Payments: has never integrated a payment provider or handled invoices, refunds or VAT.
Email and SMS at volume: has only sent email through a form plugin. Knows nothing about deliverability, sending-domain setup or sending limits.
Sign-in: has used ready-made login (Firebase Auth, Clerk). Has never built roles or permissions.
Booking widget for Calder & Finch Dental (freelance, 2025): React front end on Supabase. It shipped late because appointment reminders were added at the end.
Tiltshift, a photo-portfolio template sold on Gumroad: about 40 sales. Gumroad handled all payments and tax.
On the Calder & Finch project, reminder emails landed in spam for a week because the sending domain was not set up. The client noticed before I did.
I tend to design every screen before checking what the backend service actually allows.
Wants running costs under €30 a month until there are paying users.
Prefers managed services to running own servers.

B.summary: Backend and cloud-experienced builder. New to mobile and to marketing.

records.text: Backend: Python and FastAPI for 5 years. PostgreSQL, background jobs and REST APIs in production.
Cloud and operations: Docker, Linux servers, CI/CD and monitoring. Has been on call.
Payments: integrated Stripe subscriptions once for a business tool, including webhooks. Has never handled consumer refunds or app-store billing.
Mobile: has never shipped an iOS or Android app or been through app-store review.
Marketing and launch: has never run a launch, a waiting list or paid ads. Has no audience.
Frontend: can build plain React pages. Weak at design and accessibility.
Call-summary service at Harrowby Telecom (employee, 2024 to 2026): a speech-to-text pipeline handling 2 million minutes a month.
Ledgerline, a side project for freelancers' invoices: built for 4 months, reached 3 users, then stopped.
Ledgerline was a finished product with nobody to show it to. I started talking to users only after building.
At Harrowby an AI provider changed its rate limits with two weeks' notice and our batch jobs failed. I now check limits and deprecation dates first.
Budget for the first six months is €1,200 in total, own money.
Prefers boring, well-documented technology. Self-hosts when it is cheaper.
